content.text:
`MB_DB_FILE` sets the path of the H2 file that Metabase uses as its application database.

**Backend**
- The default value is `metabase.db` ([config/core.clj:50](src/metabase/config/core.clj#L50)).
- [app_db/env.clj:71-77](src/metabase/app_db/env.clj#L71-L77) changes the path to an absolute `file:/...` H2 path. If `MB_DB_IN_MEMORY` is set, Metabase does not use the file. It uses `mem:metabase` instead.
- Metabase uses this value only when the app DB type is H2. If `MB_DB_CONNECTION_URI` or `MB_DB_TYPE` selects Postgres or MySQL, Metabase does not use `MB_DB_FILE`.
- Some CLI commands (`load-from-h2`, `dump-to-h2`, and the encryption commands) use the same value through `mdb/db-file`.

**E2E (Cypress)**
- [cypress-runner-backend.js:31](e2e/runner/cypress-runner-backend.js#L31): if you do not set `MB_DB_FILE`, the runner sets it to a temporary file: `$TMPDIR/metabase-test-<pid>.db`.
- When the backend stops, the runner deletes `<file>.mv.db` and `<file>.trace.db` ([line 111-113](e2e/runner/cypress-runner-backend.js#L111-L113)).
- The `:e2e` alias in [deps.edn:385](deps.edn#L385) sets `mb.db.type=h2` and makes the connection URI empty. This makes sure that the backend uses `MB_DB_FILE`. The comment there says that `MB_DB_FILE` and `MB_JETTY_PORT` are the only two values that you can still change.
- The snapshot creators (for example, `default.cy.snap.js`) do not read `MB_DB_FILE`. They make snapshots through the testing API, and those snapshots are copies of this app DB.

**Other uses**
- [bin/docker/run_metabase.sh:91](bin/docker/run_metabase.sh#L91): the default in Docker is `/metabase.db`. The script can move the file to a new folder and then set `MB_DB_FILE` again.
- [mage/jar_download.clj:269](mage/src/mage/jar_download.clj#L269): each downloaded JAR version gets its own `metabase_<version>.db`.
- [.env.example:115](.env.example#L115) shows an example value: `./e2e/tmp/cypress-test.db`.

(set! *warn-on-reflection* true)

;; EVERYTHING BELOW IS FOR H2 ONLY.

(def ^:private llm-provider-fixture-schema
  ;; Keep the outer map closed; config keys are allowlisted below before persistence.
  [:map {:closed true}
   [:key ms/NonBlankString]
   [:type ms/NonBlankString]
   [:name ms/NonBlankString]
   [:config (ms/string-keyed-map [:maybe :string])]])

(defn- validate-llm-provider-fixture!
  [{:keys [type config]}]
  (let [provider-type (llm.provider/provider-type type)
        known-fields  (into (set (:stored-config-fields provider-type)) (map :key) (:fields provider-type))
        unknown-fields (remove known-fields (keys config))]
    (api/check-400 provider-type (str "Unknown provider type " (pr-str type) "."))
    (api/check-400 (empty? unknown-fields)
                   (str "Unknown " type " provider config fields: " (pr-str (vec unknown-fields)) "."))
    (llm.provider/validate-config! type config)))

(defn- assert-h2 [app-db]
  (assert (= (:db-type app-db) :h2)
          "Snapshot/restore only works for :h2 application databases."))

(defn- snapshot-path-for-name
  ^String [snapshot-name]
  (let [path (u.files/get-path "e2e" "snapshots"
                               (str (str/replace (name snapshot-name) #"\W" "_") ".sql"))]
    (str (.toAbsolutePath path))))

;;;; SAVE

(defn- save-snapshot! [snapshot-name]
  (assert-h2 (mdb/app-db))
  (let [path (snapshot-path-for-name snapshot-name)]
    (log/infof "Saving snapshot to %s" path)
    (jdbc/query {:datasource (mdb/app-db)} ["SCRIPT TO ?" path]))
  :ok)

;; TODO (Cam 2025-11-25) please add a response schema to this API endpoint, it makes it easier for our customers to
;; use our API + we will need it when we make auto-TypeScript-signature generation happen
;;
(api.macros/defendpoint :post "/snapshot/:name"
  "Snapshot the database for testing purposes."
  [{snapshot-name :name} :- [:map {:closed true}
                             [:name ms/NonBlankString]]]
  (task.search-index/wait-for-init!)
  (search.ingestion/wait-for-idle!)
  (save-snapshot! snapshot-name)
  nil)

;;;; RESTORE

(defn- reset-app-db-connection-pool!
  "Immediately destroy all open connections in the app DB connection pool."
  []
  (let [data-source (mdb/data-source)]
    (when (instance? PoolBackedDataSource data-source)
    ;; the generated snapshot has the `CREATE VIEW` *before* the `CREATE TABLE`. This results in a view that can't be
    ;; queried successfully until it is recompiled. Our workaround is to recompile ALL views immediately after we
    ;; restore the app DB from a snapshot. Bug report is here: https://github.com/h2database/h2database/issues/3942
    (doseq [table-name
            (->> (jdbc/query {:connection conn} ["SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.views WHERE table_schema=?" "PUBLIC"])
                 (map :table_name))]
      ;; parameterization doesn't work with view names. If someone maliciously named a table, this is bad. On the
      ;; other hand, this is not running in prod and you already had to have enough access to maliciously name the
      ;; table, so this is probably safe enough.
      (jdbc/execute! {:connection conn} (format "ALTER VIEW %s RECOMPILE" table-name)))))

(defn- restore-snapshot! [snapshot-name]
  (assert-h2 (mdb/app-db))
  (let [path                         (snapshot-path-for-name snapshot-name)
        ^ReentrantReadWriteLock lock (:lock (mdb/app-db))]
    ;; acquire the application DB WRITE LOCK which will prevent any other threads from getting any new connections until
    ;; we release it.
    (try
      (.. lock writeLock lock)
      (reset-app-db-connection-pool!)
      (restore-app-db-from-snapshot! path)
      (mdb/increment-app-db-unique-indentifier!)
      (finally
        (.. lock writeLock unlock)
        ;; don't know why this happens but when I try to test things locally with `bun run test-cypress-open-no-backend`
        ;; and a backend server started with `dev/start!` the snapshots are always missing columns added by DB
        ;; migrations. So let's just check and make sure it's fully up to date in this scenario. Not doing this outside
        ;; of dev because it seems to work fine for whatever reason normally and we don't want tests taking 5 million
        ;; years to run because we're wasting a bunch of time initializing Liquibase and checking for unrun migrations
        ;; for every test when we don't need to. -- Cam
        ;;
        ;; Important! This needs to happen AFTER we unlock the app DB, otherwise migrations will hang for the evil ones
        ;; that are initializing Quartz and opening new connections to do stuff on different threads.
        (when config/is-dev?
          (mdb/migrate! (mdb/app-db) :up)))))
  :ok)

;; TODO (Cam 2025-11-25) please add a response schema to this API endpoint, it makes it easier for our customers to
;; use our API + we will need it when we make auto-TypeScript-signature generation happen
;;
(api.macros/defendpoint :post "/restore/:name"
  "Restore a database snapshot for testing purposes."
  [{snapshot-name :name} :- [:map {:closed true}
                             [:name ms/NonBlankString]]]
  ;; reset the system clock, in case `/set-time` was called without cleanup
  (alter-var-root #'java-time.clock/*clock* (constantly nil))
  (.clear ^Queue @#'search.ingestion/queue)
  (restore-snapshot! snapshot-name)
  (search/sync-from-restored-db!)
  nil)

;; TODO (Cam 2025-11-25) please add a response schema to this API endpoint, it makes it easier for our customers to
;; use our API + we will need it when we make auto-TypeScript-signature generation happen
;;
(api.macros/defendpoint :post "/echo"
  "Simple echo handler. Fails when you POST with `?fail=true`."

content.text:
The snapshot creators are normal Cypress specs. The runner runs them as a separate Cypress run, after the backend starts and before the real specs.

**1. A separate Cypress config selects them**

[cypress-snapshots.config.js](e2e/support/cypress-snapshots.config.js) uses the shared default config, but sets `specPattern: "e2e/snapshot-creators/**/*.cy.snap.js"`. A run with this config runs only `default.cy.snap.js` and `qa-db.cy.snap.js`.

**2. Local runs**

In [run_cypress_local.ts:88-104](e2e/runner/run_cypress_local.ts#L88-L104), the order is:
1. The runner starts the backend (from source or from a JAR).
2. If `GENERATE_SNAPSHOTS` is true (the default), the runner:
   - deletes `e2e/support/cypress_sample_instance_data.json`
   - runs Cypress with the snapshot config, with the GUI off
   - for component tests, adds `grepTags: "-@external"`. This skips `qa-db.cy.snap.js`, which has the tag `@external`.
3. Then the runner runs the real specs with `cypress.config.js`.

If you set `GENERATE_SNAPSHOTS=false`, the runner does not make new snapshots. It shows a list of the files that are already in `e2e/snapshots`.

**3. CI runs**

[run_cypress_ci.js](e2e/runner/run_cypress_ci.js#L48-L53) has a `snapshot` command that uses the same snapshot config. The workflows call it in a step before the test step. For example, [e2e-test.yml:188-191](.github/workflows/e2e-test.yml#L188-L191) has this step:

```
node e2e/runner/run_cypress_ci.js snapshot
```

Some workflows (SDK component tests, host sample apps, pre-release) add `--spec "e2e/snapshot-creators/default.cy.snap.js"`. These workflows do not need the QA DB snapshots, so they run only the default creator.

**4. How snapshots go from the creators to the specs**

- The creators set up the app DB step by step. After each state, they call `H.snapshot("name")`. This sends `POST /api/testing/snapshot/:name`.
- The backend runs the H2 command `SCRIPT TO e2e/snapshots/<name>.sql` ([testing_api/api.clj:73-78](src/metabase/testing_api/api.clj#L73-L78)). This writes a SQL dump of the H2 app DB (the `MB_DB_FILE` database).
- The real specs call `H.restore("default")` (or another name). This sends `POST /api/testing/restore/:name`. The backend locks the app DB, clears the connection pool, and loads the `.sql` file into the DB again.

These endpoints work only when the app DB is H2. Because of this, the `:e2e` alias sets `mb.db.type=h2`.

The snapshot and the real specs must use the same backend, or a backend that has the same `e2e/snapshots` folder. The backend writes the files to a path relative to its working directory.

Yes, but only `qa-db.cy.snap.js` does this. `default.cy.snap.js` does not touch Postgres or MySQL.

Also, the setup files do not start the Postgres or MySQL servers. These servers must already run as Docker QA containers. In CI, the workflow starts them (`postgres: true`, `mysql: true`, `mongo: true` in [e2e-test.yml](.github/workflows/e2e-test.yml)). On a local machine, you must start them yourself. `qa-db.cy.snap.js` has the tag `@external`, so runs that skip that tag do not make these snapshots.

## What `qa-db.cy.snap.js` does

Look at [qa-db.cy.snap.js](e2e/snapshot-creators/qa-db.cy.snap.js). For Postgres and MySQL, it does these steps:

1. It restores `default` and adds the QA database as a Metabase database (`addPostgresDatabase()`). Then it saves the `postgres-12` snapshot.
2. `convertToWritable("postgres")`:
   - `setupWritableDB` connects to the real Postgres server through a Cypress task. If no database with the name `writable_db` exists, it runs `CREATE DATABASE writable_db` ([e2e-qa-databases-helpers.js:227-246](e2e/support/helpers/e2e-qa-databases-helpers.js#L227-L246)).
   - It sends `PUT /api/database/:id` to point the Metabase database at `writable_db`. It also changes the name to "Writable Postgres12" and turns on `database-enable-actions`.
3. It saves the `postgres-writable` snapshot.

MySQL uses the same steps and makes `mysql-8` and `mysql-writable`. MySQL uses the `root` user, because only `root` has permission to create databases.

The snapshot contains only the Metabase app DB. This is the H2 dump with the database row, its connection details, and the actions setting. It does not contain the data in `writable_db`. That data stays in the Docker container.

## How specs use them

The usual pattern ([actions-on-dashboards.cy.spec.js:879-882](e2e/test/scenarios/actions/actions-on-dashboards.cy.spec.js#L879-L882)):

```js
H.restore("postgres-writable");
H.resetTestTable({ type: "postgres", table: TEST_TABLE });
cy.signInAsAdmin();
H.resyncDatabase({ dbId: WRITABLE_DB_ID, tableName: TEST_TABLE });
```

1. **`H.restore("postgres-writable")`**: if the name has `-writable`, `restore` first calls `resetWritableDb` ([e2e-setup-helpers.js:25-29](e2e/support/helpers/e2e-setup-helpers.js#L25-L29)). This Cypress task ([db_tasks.js:41-87](e2e/support/db_tasks.js#L41-L87)) cleans the real `writable_db`:
   - Postgres: it drops all schemas except `public` and `pg_*`, and it drops all tables in `public`.
   - MySQL: it drops all tables in `writable_db`.

   Then it loads the app DB snapshot.
2. **`H.resetTestTable(...)`**: creates a known test table with seed data in `writable_db` (`resetTable` in `db_tasks.js`).
3. **`H.resyncDatabase({ dbId: WRITABLE_DB_ID })`**: Metabase does not know about the new table yet, so the spec syncs the schema. `WRITABLE_DB_ID` is `2` ([cypress_data.js:209](e2e/support/cypress_data.js#L209)). It is `2` because the writable DB is the first database that the snapshot adds after the Sample Database (ID `1`).
4. Then the spec runs actions, uploads, or other features that write data. To read or write the data directly, specs use `H.queryWritableDB(sql, type)`.

About 47 spec files under `e2e/test` use these helpers. Most of them are action, upload, and data-editing tests.

## Things to know

- The connection details come from `WRITABLE_DB_CONFIG` ([cypress_data.js:211-230](e2e/support/cypress_data.js#L211-L230)). They use the QA ports and the database name `writable_db`. The Node Cypress tasks and the Metabase backend must connect to the same server.
- All specs share one `writable_db` per server. Isolation between specs comes only from the reset in `restore`. If two runs use the same QA container at the same time, they can affect each other.
- The `mongo-5`, `postgres-12`, and `mysql-8` snapshots do not have writable versions. Specs use them only to read data from the QA sample data.

content.text:
Yes, it can work. But the separate Postgres must look the same as the QA container, seen from the Metabase backend, and the artifact must match the backend that loads it.

## What the snapshot contains

The `postgres-writable` snapshot is only an H2 dump of the Metabase app DB. For the Postgres database, it stores:

- the connection details that [addQADatabase](e2e/support/helpers/e2e-qa-databases-helpers.js#L66-L100) set: `host: localhost`, `port: 5404`, `user: metabase`, `password: metasample123`, `dbname: writable_db`
- the synced metadata (table and field rows, with their IDs) from when qa-db ran
- the database ID (`2`, which is `WRITABLE_DB_ID`)

It does not contain any Postgres data and it does not create any Postgres objects. When you restore it, Metabase only connects to whatever server is at `localhost:5404/writable_db`.

## Requirements for a separately set up Postgres

1. **Same address and credentials.** The backend and the Cypress Node tasks must both reach it at `localhost:5404` with `metabase` / `metasample123`. Both read these values from [cypress_data.js](e2e/support/cypress_data.js#L179-L230), and the snapshot also contains them. If you change the host or port, the snapshot points to the wrong server. You must then change the snapshot, or send `PUT /api/database/2` after the restore.
2. **`writable_db` must exist.** Only `setupWritableDB` creates it, and only qa-db (and some specs) call `setupWritableDB`. If qa-db does not run on this runner, nothing creates it. Then `restore("postgres-writable")` fails at once, because `resetWritableDb` connects to `writable_db` before it loads the snapshot. To prevent this, create `writable_db` when you set up the server (an init script, or `CREATE DATABASE writable_db`). After that, nothing else is necessary, because `resetWritableDb` + `resetTestTable` + `resyncDatabase` rebuild the tables for each spec.
3. **For `postgres-12` (read-only), the data must be the same.** Specs that use `postgres-12` depend on the synced metadata in the snapshot. They do not sync again. If the separate server does not use the same `metabase/qa-databases:postgres-sample-12` image, table and field IDs, field values, and query results can be different from what the specs expect.

## Requirements for the artifact

If qa-db runs in a different job and you restore its `.sql` files from an artifact, these things are important:

1. **File location.** `restore` reads `e2e/snapshots/<name>.sql` relative to the backend's working directory ([api.clj:66-70](src/metabase/testing_api/api.clj#L66-L70)). You must put the files in that folder before the specs start. CI does not upload or download snapshot artifacts now. Each job runs `run_cypress_ci.js snapshot` itself.
2. **Same Metabase build.** The dump contains the full schema of the app DB at the version that made it. If the restoring backend is at a different commit, with new or changed migrations, the restored tables do not match the code. Outside dev mode, `restore` does not run migrations ([api.clj:148-149](src/metabase/testing_api/api.clj#L148-L149)), so you get errors such as missing columns. Make the artifact with the same JAR and use it only for that JAR.
3. **Same encryption key.** If the snapshot job uses `MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY`, the database details are encrypted. The restoring backend must use the same key, or it cannot read the connection details.
4. **Make all snapshots in one run.** qa-db starts with `restore("default")` and ends with `restore("blank")`, so it needs `default.cy.snap.js` to run first in the same job. Make all the snapshot files in one job and send them all together. Do not combine `default.sql` from one build with `postgres-writable.sql` from a different build.
5. **`cypress_sample_instance_data.json`.** The default creator writes this file and specs read it. If you send the snapshots as an artifact, include this file too, or the specs can use old IDs.

## Summary

If the snapshot job and the test job use the same JAR and the same encryption key, and the test runner has a Postgres at `localhost:5404` that has `writable_db` (and the QA sample data, for `postgres-12`), the artifact works. If one of these is different, the restore fails, or tests fail in ways that are hard to understand.
what artifacts are created by default.cy.snap.js?

[default.cy.snap.js](e2e/snapshot-creators/default.cy.snap.js) makes 4 app DB snapshots and 2 JSON files. ## App DB snapshots (in `e2e/snapshots/`) The backend writes each one as an H2 SQL dump: `e2e/snapshots/.sql`. Each snapshot adds to the one before it: | Snapshot | State of the app DB | |---|---| | `blank.sql` | A new instance before setup. It has only the Sample Database and no users. | | `setup.sql` | Setup is done. The admin user exists (site name "Epic Team"), and the e2e settings are set: synchronous batch updates, public sharing, SDK and modular embedding, the embedding secret key, the license banner dismissed, and the test store URL. | | `without-models.sql` | `setup`, plus:
• the groups `collection`, `data`, `readonly`, `nosql` (the spec checks that their IDs are 5–8)
• all users from `USERS`
• data and collection permissions
• the collections First > Second > Third
• the questions "Orders", "Orders, Count", and "Orders, Count, Grouped by Created At (year)", and the dashboard "Orders in a dashboard"
• the new sample tables (Accounts, Analytic Events, Feedback, Invoices) are hidden | | `default.sql` | `without-models`, plus the model "Orders Model". Most specs restore this snapshot. | The spec also checks that the sample table IDs are the same as the static IDs in `SAMPLE_DB_TABLES`. If they are different, the run fails. ## JSON files (in `e2e/support/`) 1. **`cypress_sample_database.json`**: the IDs of the Sample Database tables and fields (for example `ORDERS_ID`, `ORDERS.CREATED_AT`). The `withSampleDatabase` helper gets them from the API. Specs import them through `cypress_sample_database.js`. 2. **`cypress_sample_instance_data.json`**: data from the `default` state: - `loginCache`: the session cookies for each user. `cy.signIn` uses them, so specs do not need to log in through the API again. **These sessions are rows in the app DB in the snapshot.** They work only with the snapshots from the same run. - `questions`, `users`, `databases`, `groups`, `collections`, `dashboards`: what the API returns. Specs import these through `cypress_sample_instance_data.js` and do not hard-code the IDs. The spec gets this data **after** it saves `default`, because the API calls add rows to the audit log, and these rows must not go into the snapshot. On EE, the spec also turns on `use-tenants` for a short time, so that the "All tenant users" group is included in `groups`. It then turns it off again. At the end, the spec restores `blank`, so the backend is in a clean state for the next snapshot spec. ## Why this is important for artifacts If you send these files to a different job, send the 4 `.sql` files and the 2 JSON files together, all from the same run. `loginCache` contains session IDs that exist only in those snapshots. `qa-db.cy.snap.js` starts from `default.sql`, so you must also make its snapshots from the same set.
